questions.evidence:
Five cards wait on the review desk: label, entrance, record, collect, and preparation. Each pair must place a card beside a short situation. The teacher asks students to explain their choices before turning the cards over to check the answers.

One situation describes a student writing down how many seeds have roots. Another describes a visitor taking a repaired bag home. Hana first puts collect beside the seed situation because she imagines collecting seeds from the ground.

Her partner points to the words writing down. Hana moves record to that situation and collect to the bag situation. They put entrance beside a door description and label beside a paper with a name on it.

The final situation describes sorting materials before the real job begins. After choosing preparation, the pair writes a new example together. They learn that a familiar word still needs to fit the action described around it.
